channel.title: Los Angeles Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Los Angeles Times (latimes.com)

item.title: Little snow in California and the West as a warm winter nears end
item.description: California's snowpack remains much smaller than average after months of extremely warm conditions across the West.

item.title: Two women convicted of stalking ICE agent during Los Angeles immigration protests
item.description: Two protesters were convicted of stalking a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent in a case that could test the limits of furious protests against the Trump administration's immigration raids in Southern California.

item.title: Paramount-Warner Bros. deal stirs fears about what it means for CNN
item.description: What the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery deal means for the cable network CNN.

item.title: Lawsuit against L.A. County deputies involved in fight outside Santa Clarita bar dismissed
item.description: A lawsuit claiming that a man was beaten outside a Santa Clarita bar by off-duty Los Angeles County sheriff’s deputies, who then conspired with a high-ranking sheriff’s official to cover up the incident, was dismissed by a federal judge this week.

item.title: Bill Clinton gives House testimony on Epstein, fueling calls for Trump to do same
item.description: The closed-door deposition in Chappaqua, N.Y., marks the first time a former president has been compelled to testify to Congress. It comes a day after Clinton's wife, former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, sat with lawmakers for her own deposition.

item.title: Who will run 'El Mencho's' cartel now? It could be a man born in California
item.description: Now that the head of the Jalisco New Generation cartel is dead, what will happen to its coalition of ruthless regional commanders? Will they agree to share power? Elevate one as supreme leader? Or will a bloody power struggle break out?

item.title: Power, politics and a $2.8-billion exit: How Paramount topped Netflix to win Warner Bros.
item.description: The Ellisons and their team began plotting their comeback in December, the morning after Netflix clinched its deal to buy Warner Bros.

item.title: L.A. school board's closed-door meeting ends with no decision on Supt. Carvalho's future after FBI raid
item.description: The Los Angeles Board of Education met behind closed doors Thursday night, a day after federal authorities raided the home and office of Supt. Alberto Carvalho in what appears to be a probe related to AllHere.

item.title: Carvalho's big bet on AI imploded at L.A. schools. Now, it's the center of FBI raids
item.description: Rather than go with a major player, LAUSD chose a small startup to develop an AI chatbot for students. How it all unraveled, culminating in FBI raids on the superintendent.

item.title: LAUSD Supt. Alberto Carvalho placed on paid leave following FBI raid of home, office
item.description: The LAUSD school board moved quickly to put Supt. Alberto Carvalho on paid administrative leave two days after the FBI raided his home and office.
